study_note: Seed-55 single-training-seed exploratory one-million-decision Humanoid Walk value-equivalence-loss screen; one seed does not support a confidence or significance claim. Relative to the matched q5/pair2 seed-55 control, the only learning-axis change is the continuing-task successor-value equivalence loss with coefficient 0.1 and four Monte Carlo samples per update. Both prior-writeback coefficients remain zero, explicit value-equivalence diagnostics remain disabled, and the active loss itself logs raw, weighted, and per-depth terms each update. The distributional critic retains five heads, every actor and target reduction samples two distinct heads and takes their minimum, both critic targets remain reward-only, and automatic outer temperature tuning retains the normalized rho-weighted actor-depth mixture. At step zero and every 50,000 decisions, observational evaluation runs the 100-sample fixed-seed Q-versus-MC protocols and five seed-12345 paired real-environment episodes comparing deterministic outer control with deterministic execution after a fresh action-local inner SAC solve at every state. The primary real improvement signal is eval/paired_fresh_inner_minus_outer. Evaluation disables write-back, adds only separately timed probe compute, and does not consume the training decision budget. Compare against the first one million decisions of the existing seed-55 q5/pair2 base run c6857707751946929e27be0514a502a5; no inner-learning-rate-swap run is a baseline.
